title: One image in - 2D animated and customizable character out
author: floopyFx
selftext:
I've spent the last week building a ComfyUI pipeline that turns a reference image into animated, customizable character sprite sheets.

The Pipeline is split into two parts and is fully running locally on my RTX 3090 with 24GB VRAM:

**1 -** **Base Animations** **(Idle, walk, jump... etc)**

Starting with a ‘bare’ base character image - This produces a grayscale sprite sheet of my animated base character.

* **WAN 2.2 i2v 14B** (Q5\_K\_M GGUF, distilled lightx2v 4-step) is used for image to video generation
* **BiRefNet** for background strip producing clean alpha.
* **ImageStitch** and **ImageRGBToYUV** nodes for creating a grayscale sprite sheet

**2 -** **Customization layers** **(eyes, hair,  shirt... etc)**

Starting from an animated video of the base animation and an image of the customization i want to create a layer out of - This produces a grayscale sprite sheet of the customization.

* **Wan 2.1 VACE 14B** (Q5\_K\_M GGUF) + **CausVid distill LoRA** for inpainting the cosmetic over the animated video - this ensures that the cosmetic is aligned with the base animation on every frame.
* **SAM3** segmentation for isolating the customization on each frame
* **ImageStitch** and **ImageRGBToYUV** again used to produce the sprite sheet of the customization.

Each Customization needs to be re-produced for each base animation and the grayscale allows me to tint each layer separately.

The hard part was getting the customization layers to align pixel-perfectly over the base character animation.  
i initially tried **Wan 2.2 Animate** but it didn't stay true to the original base animation so i eventually went with the inpainting model instead.

Still kind of amazed I got here as someone who can hardly draw a stick figure.

replies.author: floopyFx
replies.body: Honestly, you might want to consider renting a GPU and running this on a pod. it doesn't cost as much as you might think. and regarding making this work for vehicles - i think you can start from a template vehicle instead of my template chibi character (you can generate it locally or using nono-babanana for free at https://labs.google) and than use the pipeline to create base animations for the vehicle and customization layers.

comments.author: sumane12
comments.body: Can you create a workflow for a 16gb 5060ti

replies.author: floopyFx
replies.body:
honestly, i think if i had anything less than 24 gigs i'de rent a GPU (you can rent a 96GB one for a dollar an hour, not so bad for playing around).

even on my 24 gigs i had to dynamically unload models and reload them whenever needed so the active ones always have enough VRAM wothout crashing my machine.

replies.author: FormalMaximum5168
replies.body: Yeah, running local Wan workflows on 16GB is a struggle. If you don't want to deal with renting GPUs or ComfyUI VRAM errors, you could always generate the raw character motion clips on DomoAI first, then bring them into your local editor to slice into sprite sheets.
